chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: It is not permissible for the one praying to pray while in a state of wudu unless it is from a ghusl or wudu.
Meaning: If he has prayed a prayer and fulfilled it, then he wishes to pray another prayer, he must have a new [ablution].
And it is not permissible for him to pray two prayers with one wudu, unless the wudu was from a ghusl.
ai.seo_question: Can I pray two prayers with one wudu in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) clarification that distinct obligatory prayers require separate ablitions to ensure ritual purity is maintained for each act of worship, distinguishing this from the comprehensive purification of *ghusl*. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the integrity of *wudu* as a prerequisite for valid *salah*, while acknowledging the exception where *ghusl* inherently includes the state of purity required for prayer.
